doc.title: Jerry Coker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 18, 2023

title: Closing remarks and quote from his book
summary: Coker does not listen to his recordings; Rowe reads the opening of his book and thanks him and Curt.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: You recorded a number of LPs or CDs over the years and I wonder if you ever put them on to listen to yourself?
That’s okay. Most musicians respond with the same answer. Well this has really been a joy for me, and I appreciate you taking your time today.
Right. And I enjoyed talking to you.

I’m going to close with something you wrote in the beginning of this book and this is the very first thing that you wrote. And it said, “The training, care and feeding of the jazz musician is something which many of us ought to be more concerned. For jazz is the significant and vital musical language truly of our time. Its value has increased with the years as it developed beyond its humble beginnings to become a sophisticated art form which speaks an international world-wide language.”
That sounds great. I’d like to use that in a book sometime.

Well I’m going to give you permission. You know it was prescient at the time but it’s still profound, Mr. Coker, so as I said, thank you for your time, and thank Curt, your son, for helping us out here. And I appreciate it very much.
Okay. I enjoyed it and I enjoyed meeting you.
Likewise. We’ll do a virtual handshake.
All right there you go. Thank you very much.
